instructions.content: Mode A splits a legacy source into its own dated sections and emits one journal-entry-creator-compatible file per non-empty section, preserving content verbatim and normalising only formatting.

Mode B fetches the ticket with comments, applies the 'enough data' bar (skip a ticket with nothing to narrate), dates the detail entry by the ticket's resolution date (fallback: last-updated, then the mentioning entry's date), and cross-links it back to the mentioning entry with plain markdown.

NEVER set refinement_ticket on a ticket-detail entry - it makes journal-entry-creator's base validator require a '## Proposed Ticket Description' section, which does not apply to a closed historical ticket. Put the ticket link in source and the metadata block only.

NEVER invent a frontmatter field (e.g. continues_from/continued_by) to express the cross-link between a detail entry and the entry that mentioned it - tekhne's base frontmatter schema has no such field. Use plain-markdown bidirectional links instead.

NEVER redact colleague names on your own judgement - ask the author first. The exceptions you do not ask about first: never write credentials/tokens/passwords into the repo (mask them), and summarise out bulk end-user/customer identifiers and raw data dumps.

Write the Decisions and Resolution section as a synthesised narrative of what was decided and how it resolved, not a per-comment transcript. Add the '> **Decisive contribution (<name>):**' callout only when the author was the pivotal actor; omit it on team efforts.

In a batch run, NEVER trust an agent's 'written' status without confirming the file exists on disk, and NEVER stage only the batch's own year directory - resolution-date dating can land a file in a different year, so stage every year directory the batch touched.

For migrated external links (Mode C), annotate - keep the original archived URL and append the resolved current home. Deep links (PR numbers, commits) do not translate; point to the repo root. A repo-mapping manifest entry that still points at the old host means the repo was NOT migrated.

This skill is for reconstructing entries from external systems, not for repairing frontmatter on entries that already exist in the repo's format - that is pantheon-journal's own 'backfill' command. Do not treat an in-repo frontmatter-repair request as a Mode A/B/C task.
